notes: One capture that answers 'does the Rust TUI actually do codex/pi-style interaction?' with the real binary.

Panels walk the interactive surface: startup frame → /settings (6 rows, LUM-1310) → Esc back to the composer → /help reference block → /hotkeys keybinding table → fuzzy `/set` filtering over the slash-command set.

Uses the repo's established harness idiom: `<C-u>` (Ctrl+U, clear the composer line) before each command and `<Esc>` to close an overlay, matching scripts/pty_scenarios/lum1267-interaction-assertions.json. A bare `/` after a previous command is racy — an earlier version of this file did that and the /settings panel rendered a reset transcript.
Every panel asserts on the character grid, so a regression turns this into a FAIL rather than a silently different picture.

Honest note on the /help panel: the reference block is bottom-anchored, so in 120x34 only its tail is on screen — `/settings` (near the top of the command list) is NOT visible there. The panel asserts `/help` only; `/settings` is asserted where it belongs, via `/set` filtering in panel 6 and the modal in panel 2.
caption: LUM-1310 — the pi-rust TUI interaction surface, real binary + real PTY (120x34) + pyte. Panel 1: startup frame with the key-hint header and composer. Panel 2: `/settings` with the six wired rows (LUM-1310 added the last three). Panel 3: Esc closes the modal and the composer is restored. Panel 4: `/help` reference block (source-line-aware wrapping). Panel 5: `/hotkeys` chord table. Panel 6: `/set` fuzzy-filters the slash-command set down to `settings`. Nothing mocked.

panels.label: 1. idle — startup header + composer + status bar
2. /settings — the six wired rows (LUM-1310 added Hide thinking / Autocomplete max items / Quiet startup)
3. Esc — the settings modal closes and the composer is back
4. /help — command reference block, wrapped per source line (bottom-anchored: only the tail is visible in 120x34)
5. /hotkeys — the chord table including the app.* section
6. `/set` — fuzzy slash-command filtering narrows the list to `settings`
